notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Source is the FY2025 Annual Report on Form 20-F as filed on EDGAR (February 26, 2026, accession 0001104659-26-020058); dividends, buybacks and stock comp match SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0001000184). EUR, converted exactly from € millions. LEADER: Hasso Plattner, a cofounder, left the Supervisory Board on May 15, 2024; the FY2025 20-F mentions him only in historical compensation tables (as Supervisory Board chairperson until May 15, 2024, and as a former Executive Board member). Its major-shareholder table (as of February 5, 2026) covers 5% holders and current board members only and does not list him, his foundation or family vehicles. No holding is reported, so status is 'no-reported-stake'. This does not mean he holds no SAP shares; the filing simply gives no figure. HOLDERS: percentages are '% of Outstanding' ordinary shares as reported to SAP. Dietmar Hopp's 5.1% rests on a Schedule 13G filed February 11, 2022, and BlackRock's 6.3% on a 13G filed February 2, 2024 (BlackRock told SAP it still holds more than 5% but gave no count); asOf uses those filing dates because the 20-F gives no event dates. Dietmar Hopp is another SAP cofounder, not part of Plattner's holdings. BUYBACKS: €1,937 million 'Purchase of treasury shares' in the 2025 cash-flow statement. SAP announced a new buyback of up to €10 billion in January 2026, after the fiscal year. STOCK COMP: €1,695 million total share-based payment expense (equity- and cash-settled). GEOGRAPHY: the six country/sub-region rows; EMEA, Americas and APJ subtotals are not repeated.

marketcap.notes: One class of ordinary bearer shares, priced from the primary listing on Xetra/Frankfurt (SAP.DE, EUR) rather than the NYSE ADR (SAP, 1 ADR = 1 share). Shares = 1,228.5 million issued − 74.3 million treasury = 1,154.2 million at June 30, 2026, from the Half-Year Report 2026 equity note, which states both parts (rounded to 0.1 million) but not the difference. The 20-F cover count (1,228,504,232 at December 31, 2025, including 60,945,184 treasury shares) is not used because SAP has been buying back heavily under its €10 billion program announced in January 2026; the Q3 2026 statement (October 26, 2026) gives 25,205,983 shares repurchased under the program by September 30, 2026, against 16.3 million by June 30, but no share count, so the edition-date count is somewhat lower than recorded.
